lesson: In assetserve's content_type lookup, use a deterministic in-code pinned table instead of calling Python's mimetypes.guess_type or relying on OS registries.
why: mimetypes reads platform-specific OS registries, causing inconsistent MIME resolution across different machines and environments.
quote: mimetypes reads the OS registry, which is exactly why the symptom is 'some users': the answer differs per machine and per platform.

lesson: In the content_type table, map .csv strictly to text/csv, rejecting application/vnd.ms-excel.
why: Serving application/vnd.ms-excel mangles Excel's import path for analytics CSV exports.
quote: application/vnd.ms-excel is a Windows-registry fossil, and it's what mangles the Excel import path for the analytics exports.

lesson: Telemetry for unknown file extensions in assetserve must use a counter metric rather than per-request logging.
why: High-volume asset traffic serving millions of files daily would overwhelm the log collector if unknown extensions triggered log lines.
quote: the asset host serves millions of files a day and per-request logging for unknowns would drown the collector

lesson: Extension matching in content_type must be case-insensitive by lowercasing the file extension before matching against lowercase table keys.
why: Real-world uploads and legacy shares frequently arrive with uppercase or mixed-case extensions such as .JPG, .CSV, and .Html.
quote: Camera uploads arrive as .JPG, the analytics exporter emits .CSV, and the old Windows share is full of .Html. Lowercase the extension

lesson: Map .svg to exactly 'image/svg+xml; charset=utf-8' with the charset suffix included, rejecting bare image/svg+xml.
why: Serving SVG markup without an explicit charset was identified as an XSS vulnerability during a penetration test.
quote: it came out of the XSS pentest finding - svg is markup, and serving it without an explicit charset was part of the reported attack surface.

lesson: Map .js to text/javascript instead of application/javascript in the content_type table.
why: text/javascript aligns with the modern WHATWG registry standard.
quote: .js is text/javascript per the WHATWG registry, not application/javascript.

lesson: Map both .yaml and .yml extensions to application/x-yaml in the content_type table.
why: Configuration templates use both file extension spellings across different pipelines.
quote: Half the config templates use the short form; a table that only knows one spelling is how we get another 'works on my pipeline' ticket.

lesson: Set the fallback MIME type for unmapped or unknown extensions in content_type to application/octet-stream, rejecting text/plain.
why: A text/plain fallback causes browsers to display sensitive leaked build artifacts inline instead of forcing a download.
quote: the text/plain fallback is why the browser displayed that leaked build artifact inline instead of forcing a download.

lesson: In content_type filename parsing, treat single-dot files (.env), extensionless names, and trailing-dot names as having no extension (falling back to application/octet-stream), while multi-dot files (.config.yaml) resolve by their final extension.
why: This distinction ensures sensitive standalone dotfiles fall back to octet-stream for safety, while configuration files with true extensions map appropriately.
quote: a dotfile with NO other dot - .env, .gitignore - has no extension at all, so octet-stream. A dot-leading name WITH a real extension
